paragraphs.text: Manage MCP servers from a left sidebar panel in DSH instead of YAML
# MCP servers for DSH
Manage MCP servers from a panel in the DSH left sidebar instead of hand-editing the profile's YAML.
中文说明
## What it gives you
- A **MCP servers** entry in the left sidebar. It opens a full page in the main column, so server st

ate is one click away instead of buried in Settings.
- The same editor on **Settings → MCP servers**

and **Plugins → MCP servers → Configure**.
- **stdio** servers (a local command) and **streamable H

TTP** servers (a URL).
- **Test connection** before saving: performs the MCP handshake and lists the

tools the server exposes.
- Per-server enable switch, live status (connected / connecting / failed)

and per-call timeout (1–600 s, default 60 s).
- **Secrets stay out of configuration**: secret envir
onment variables and headers are stored in the DSH credential store; the row config keeps only the c

redential key name.
- A read-only agent tool, `mcp_servers` (`list` / `test`), so the model can insp
ect connection state without being able to add or change servers.
## Install

1. **Plugins → Add plugin** and paste `https://github.com/HalcyonAzure/dsh-mcp-manager`.
2. Click **

MCP servers** in the left sidebar (or open **Settings → MCP servers**).
3. **Add server**, fill in t
he connection, **Test connection**, **Save**.
Saving restarts the plugin row, so every server reconnects and any in-flight MCP call is interrupted
aving restarts the plugin row, so every server reconnects and any in-flight MCP call is interrupted.
Requires a DSH build that provides the `sidebar.panellist` and `main` slots plus the `@deepseek-ai/d
sh-mcp-client` package — any current DSH release has them.
## Add a server
### stdio (local program)
| Field | Meaning |

| Name | Letters, digits, `-`, `_`; up to 32 characters. Becomes the tool-name prefix. |
| Command |

Absolute path or command name, for example `npx` or `/usr/local/bin/my-server`. |
| Arguments | One

argument per line. |
| Environment variables | Plain, non-secret values. |
| Secret environment var

iables | Credential key + value; the value goes to the DSH credential store. |
| Working directory |

dential key + value; the value goes to the DSH credential store. |
| Working directory | Optional. |
### streamable HTTP (remote service)
| Field | Meaning |

| Name | Same rule as above. |
| URL | `http://` or `https://` endpoint of the MCP server. |
| Heade

rs | Plain request headers. |
| Secret headers | Credential key + value, stored in the credential st

lain request headers. |
| Secret headers | Credential key + value, stored in the credential store. |
Leave a secret value empty to keep the value that is already stored.
### Row status
Each row shows a dot and a tool count: **connected** (green), **connecting** (amber), **failed** or
**not connected** (red), **disabled** (grey). A failure prints the server's own error text under the
connected** (red), **disabled** (grey). A failure prints the server's own error text under the row.
## How it works
- **Host half** (index.js) keeps the server list in its own row config, mounts one `@deepseek-ai/dsh
-mcp-client` child per enabled server, and serves two local endpoints to the UI: `api/mcp-manager.se

rvers` and `api/mcp-manager.test`.
- **Client half** (client.js) registers the sidebar entry, the ma
in panel, the Settings section and the plugin row page. It is plain JavaScript loaded through the DS

H client module loader, so there is no build step.
- Tool names keep the MCP convention: `mcp__<serv
er-name>__<tool-name>`.
## Configuration
The server list belongs to this plugin's row. The UI writes it through the DSH config editor; it can
also be written directly in the profile patch:

## Security notes
- A stdio server runs the command you configure, with **your** user account and your machine's permi

ssions. Only add servers you trust.
- Adding, editing and deleting servers is user-only in the UI; t

he agent tool cannot change configuration.
- Ambient `*KEY*`, `*PASSWORD*`, `*SECRET*`, `*TOKEN*` an

d `DSH_*` variables are scrubbed from the environment handed to a stdio server.
- Secret values are
resolved when the plugin mounts; a missing secret is reported on the row rather than silently substi
ed when the plugin mounts; a missing secret is reported on the row rather than silently substituted.
## Development
The plugin is plain ESM plus a plain client module — no bundler, no dependencies. Install the checko
ut as a local bundle (**Plugins → Add plugin** with the directory path), edit files, reload the page
